sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球海事商船注册旗国、借鉴特拉华州公司法的非公开发行实体

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Automated Global Payroll and Staff Compliance Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law; corporate law modeled on the Delaware General Corporation Law with indigenous land-law exceptions
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty of Free Association between the Republic of the Marshall Islands and the United States of America (1986, amended 2003)
Hague Convention Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents (HCCH 1961, effective for the Republic of the Marshall Islands as of 14 December 2023)
United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime (UNTOC)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Marshall Islands Revised Code, Title 113, Business Corporations Act; Business Corporation (Beneficial Ownership Information) Regulation 2022; Financial Institutions Regulation Act 2020 (FIRA 2020); AML/CFT Act (Title 75) and subsequent amendments; Financial Intelligence Unit regulations and reporting directives

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarially certified copy of passport and proof of identity for each ultimate beneficial owner, director and authorised signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public / competent issuing authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the origin country is party to HCCH 1961; otherwise full consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified proof of residential address or bank statement for each shareholder and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed financial institution in country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization depending on origin jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing the Marshall Islands registered agent for filing and service of process
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public legitimated in the Marshall Islands or foreign notary with apostille
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille / consular legalization of foreign signatures

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance / certificate of good conduct for each director and ultimate beneficial owner, with English translation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police or government background-check authority of the person's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if applicable; otherwise consular legalization; notarized English translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank and professional reference letter confirming source of funds and professional standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or regulated financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal AML verification by registered agent; formal legalization not normally required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners and authorised signatories against OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, Marshall Islands domestic sanctions notices, UK, EU, Australia and China sanctions lists, and FATF/APG public statements. Politically Exposed Persons and their family members and close associates require enhanced due diligence, documented source-of-wealth review and risk-based transaction monitoring through the Marshall Islands Financial Intelligence Unit under FIRA 2020 and Title 75 AML/CFT rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Marshall Islands Business, Companies and Maritime Registry (BCMR) Online Services Portal, filed through a licensed registered agent
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_dokumend: Company names must be submitted in Latin-script English characters. The Marshalls Official language (Kajin Majel) and English are both official; non-Roman script names must be transliterated and accompanied by a certified English translation. Suffixes must be one of: Limited, Corporation, Incorporated, LTD, LLC or a statutory equivalent. Names must not be misleading or imply a relationship with the Republic of the Marshall Islands government without express ministerial consent.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to the Registrar of Corporations within 14 calendar days of the rejection notice, attaching revised name documentation or addressing the stated ground of refusal. If reconsideration fails, the applicant may file an administrative appeal to the Business, Companies and Maritime Registry appellate panel within 21 calendar days. The final judicial remedy is an application to the High Court of the Marshall Islands under Title 113 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code. A name reservation may be extended by filing a renewal request before expiration of the initial 30-day window, subject to BCMR administrative fees.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Fully permitted for a non-resident Business Corporation in the software / payroll-as-a-service industry. The registered agent's office address in Majuro may serve as the statutory registered office; no local physical business premises are required. A physical office is only necessary if the entity later becomes a licensed financial institution, maintains a substantive local payroll, or wishes to evidence economic substance under a bank's correspondent due diligence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Below 5% annual probability for a non-licensed Payroll SaaS IT entity, subject to discretionary BCMR regulatory visits and compliance audits where prior adverse indicators exist; if any licensed payment or VASP activity is added, inspection likelihood increases to over 80% with mandatory AML examination.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search and name reservation fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Business Corporations Act, Title 113, Marshall Islands Revised Code

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Business Corporation incorporation filing fee and certificate issuance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory initial capital filing tariff, BCMR fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Finance / Government of the Marshall Islands
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Annual corporate license fee mandated at incorporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent and registered office service (12 months)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Marshall Islands registered agent / corporate service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark, standard CSP package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO disclosure registry filing and ongoing record maintenance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Administrative filing charge under Business Corporation Beneficial Ownership Information Regulation 2022

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, authentication and apostille packet for corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public / competent apostille authority in document origin jurisdiction

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT PEP and sanctions screening engine fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External compliance screening platform / analytical provider

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Final pre-incorporation legal due diligence opinion and entity structure memorandum

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act, Sections 28 (Articles of Incorporation), 47 (Registered Office and Agent), 55 (Initial Directors), and 60 (Officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Business Registration Division, Ministry of Commerce and Investment, Republic of the Marshall Islands
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form BC-1) together with Initial Statement of Directors and Registered Agent
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is mandated by law; issued capital may be authorized and subscribed at par or no-par value. No escrow account requirement applies to non-resident business corporations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Board of Directors approves the subscription for the authorized shares of the corporation as set forth in the Articles of Incorporation; that the registered office and registered agent shown on the initial filing are adopted as the statutory address and agent; that the officers named in the Officer Appointment Sheet are elected to serve until the first annual meeting; that the directors are authorized to open bank accounts, execute payroll automation client agreements, and engage the registered agent; and that the corporate seal and bylaws are adopted. This resolution takes effect immediately upon signing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Business Registration Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request via the online registry portal or in person, stating the proposed corporate name and confirming the designation 'Corporation' or 'Inc.' Payment of the name reservation fee is required at filing. The registry will issue a name clearance certificate if the name is distinguishable from existing entities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is confused with a pre-existing entity, submit an alternate name or file an administrative objection with the Registrar within 14 days of the refusal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Agent (licensed Marshall Islands corporate services provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage the registered agent to prepare the Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws, Initial Statement of Directors, and Registered Agent consent. Verify that the purposes clause covers ISIC 6201 (software development and cloud payroll services) and that the capital structure references the authorized shares. Ensure all documents are in English and signed by the incorporator.
required_dossiers: Initial director and officer identification documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any drafting deficiencies identified by the registered agent and re-submit revised documents within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Articles of Incorporation with Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Business Registration Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed Articles of Incorporation with the Registrar together with the filing fee. The Registrar will examine the document for legal compliance under the Business Corporations Act. Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar returns a query, file a written amendment correcting the identified defect within 14 days; if the defect is fundamental, withdraw and re-file a revised document along with an additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Bylaws and First Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First Board of Directors (internal corporate governance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a board meeting or obtain unanimous written consent adopting the bylaws, issuing shares to subscribers, appointing officers, approving bank account opening, and granting the registered agent authority to receive legal process. Execute the pro-forma board resolution and keep minutes in the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Stock ledger and share subscription documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any director or officer appointment is rejected by the corporate records review, execute a new resolution and file an amended officer statement with the Registrar, if required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Tax Identification Number and Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tax Office, Ministry of Finance; Business License Divisions, local government
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the national Tax Identification Number (TIN) and a standard business license for the corporation. For a non-resident corporation with no physical presence and no local revenue, obtain a non-resident business license exemption certificate if applicable. Retain all registration documents for compliance.
required_dossiers: Board resolution naming the local registered agent
Business license application with zoning clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry requests additional evidence of operation, provide a sworn statement from the registered agent confirming non-resident status and the absence of a local commercial footprint.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce and Investment, Business License Office in coordination with the local municipal authority
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Business License (for commercial software service providers)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority of the Republic of the Marshall Islands
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA; administrative registration only for cloud-hosted software operations with no physical manufacturing footprint
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emissions generated by digital services; compliance with EUI and solid waste disposal rules limited to office e-waste disposal; any electronic waste must be handled through certified recycling channels as per Environment Protection Act 2020.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For office-based payroll technology operations: fire safety certificate issued by the Fire Prevention Authority; structural load inspection for server rooms, if any; and occupational health clearance for secure server rooms, requiring uninterruptible power supply and ventilation certification.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Marshall Islands Revenue and Customs Administration (RICA), Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands; corporate registry administered by the Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General. Taxpayer access through RICA services and RMI-licensed registered agents; customs declarations processed via the ASYCUDA World portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: No compulsory RMI tax identification number or VAT ID is issued to a Non-Resident Domestic Corporation (NRDC). Procedure: (1) incorporate under the Business Corporation Act 1990 through an RMI-licensed registered agent; (2) elect NRDC status in the Articles of Incorporation (BCA section 106); (3) no RMI TIN/VAT ID applies because RMI has no VAT and NRDC status places the entity outside the income and gross-revenue tax base; (4) if the entity later acquires RMI nexus (RMI premises, employees, or RMI-source customers), it must apply to RICA for a Business License and Business Taxpayer Number and register as an employer with the RMI Social Security Administration; (5) foreign vendors without RMI nexus have no registration obligation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: RMI has no check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election. The only material statutory election is the NRDC designation in the Articles of Incorporation; the designation is revocable only by charter amendment, and NRDC status is lost if the corporation carries on business within the RMI, becoming subject to Business Gross Revenue Tax and municipal business licensing.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT, GST, or sales and use tax exists in the Marshall Islands. Indirect and turnover levies comprise: (i) customs import duty under the Customs Act 1990; (ii) Business Gross Revenue Tax (BGRT) at tiered rates up to 3% of gross revenue derived from business conducted within the RMI; and (iii) municipal business license fees.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable - no VAT regime exists and therefore no VAT registration threshold applies. For BGRT, any person carrying on business in the RMI must obtain a business license before operations commence; there is no de minimis turnover exemption for a foreign digital payroll service provider with physical, employment, or other economic nexus in the RMI.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. RMI does not mandate e-invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API-based tax clearance, or digital stamping. Customs import/export declarations are filed through ASYCUDA World; BGRT returns and business license renewals are processed on an annual cycle by RICA in paper or basic electronic formats.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable - RMI has no VAT or GST, therefore no 0% export VAT rate and no input-VAT refund mechanism exists. Exports of goods are free of export duty; offshore SaaS payroll automation services supplied by an NRDC to non-resident clients fall outside the BGRT base provided the corporation has no RMI nexus. No zero-rating certificate is issued or required.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (for goods physically exported from RMI)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward Remittance or proof of payment (only where a licensing condition requires; RMI has no general foreign-exchange control)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No export-VAT clawback exists because no export zero-rating regime exists. False customs declarations attract penalties under the Customs Act 1990, including fines, forfeiture of goods, and imprisonment. BGRT non-compliance triggers a 10% late-payment penalty, monthly interest accrual, business license suspension, and retrospective assessment; an NRDC that transacts business inside the RMI loses its tax-exempt status and may be assessed for all open periods within the statutory limitation window.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: There is no domestic central bank in the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI). The U.S. Federal Reserve System acts as the de facto monetary authority for the U.S. dollar, which is the sole legal tender. The competent financial supervisory authority is the RMI Banking Commissioner, Ministry of Finance & Banking, which licenses banks and monitors foreign exchange and AML compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: RMI maintains no exchange-control legislation. Both current-account receipts and capital-account transactions are fully convertible and freely transferable in U.S. dollars. There are no statutory restrictions on profit repatriation, dividend distribution, or liquidation proceeds for non-resident business corporations, provided corporate records evidence a valid distribution declaration and continued tax-exempt status.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: RMI imposes no mandatory surrender, conversion timeline, or forced repatriation ratio for export proceeds or any other foreign-currency receipts. A non-resident business corporation may retain, pool, or disburse received funds freely. Banks in the U.S. clearing system may require invoice, bill-of-lading, or contract documentation for source-of-funds compliance, but no statutory surrender timeline applies.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium, subject to enhanced due diligence. Legal constraints: RMI does not issue fintech EMI or money transmitter licences; digital EMI providers are generally licensed in other jurisdictions (e.g., UK FCA, US OCC, EU/EEA) and may classify an RMI non-resident business corporation as high-risk due to offshore tax-exempt status, potential FATF/EU enhanced monitoring history, and nominee ownership possibilities. Many EMIs will require a genuine U.S. operating nexus, a U.S. physical address, and an EIN, which conflicts with the pure non-resident BC structure. A licensed RMI local bank or a U.S.-based EMI with a transparent BO registry and real office presence is the preferred workaround.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For Bank of Marshall Islands, Inc., directors and authorized signatories must appear physically at a Majuro or Ebeye branch for the original KYC interview; remote opening is not accepted. For an offshore fintech EMI, remote video onboarding is sometimes permitted, but the RMI beneficial owners must provide apostilled notarized copies, certified passport and proof of address, and, in certain cases, complete an in-person verification at a U.S. embassy or consulate. A U.S. correspondent bank will usually demand an in-person board attendance at one of its offices or a verified digital interview with a notary present.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore non-resident business corporation with tax-exempt status and no physical footprint in the jurisdiction of residence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete beneficial ownership register, corporate register extract, certificate of good standing, board resolution confirming no local tax residence, audited financial statements or an independent tax-exempt status opinion, OECD-compliant economic substance policy, physical office lease or U.S. operating nexus evidence, and designation of an AML compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume multi-jurisdictional payroll and contractor disbursements characteristic of a payroll SaaS platform
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid money transmitter / MSB registration in the operating jurisdiction, detailed transaction monitoring and sanctions screening policy, underlying payroll and service contracts for expected payment flows, evidence of ACH and SWIFT partner banks, SOC 2 Type II report, and a published transaction limit and threshold structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Funds originating from a foreign founder or shareholder without transparent source-of-wealth records
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SWIFT MT103 evidence from the sending bank, three years of personal or corporate bank statements, tax returns or tax status certificate, independent asset and wealth report, notarized share subscription and gift or sale agreements, and a UBO certification containing passport, proof of address, and professional references.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing uses SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder’s bank to the RMI bank account or an approved U.S.-based EMI corporate account, with the remitter name exactly matching the recorded beneficial owner. The payment reference must state 'CAPITAL INJECTION — SHARE SUBSCRIPTION — MH_BC' and must include the entity ID. Supporting documentation: board resolution approving the share issuance, share subscription agreement, register of members, certification of beneficial ownership, and source-of-funds statement. No exchange-control approval is required. If routed through New York Fedwire, the receiving U.S. intermediary will require a valid ABA/routing number, confirmed sanctions screening, and active account validation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Treasury outflows for payroll automation settle through SWIFT MT103 for high-value or cross-border vendor payments; low-value recurring payroll is batched through the platform’s licensed ACH and SEPA clearing partners. For significant software-implementation and infrastructure contracts, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit (UCP600) is permissible, with a silent confirmation option when the LC issuing bank is not a quality-of-name institution. A standby LC may be used for performance or service guarantees. Foreign-currency disbursements are executed after a spot FX transaction with a correspondent bank, then cleared via MT103 in the target currency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statement and Annual Franchise Tax Payment (non-resident Business Corporation minimum statutory tier; graduated franchise tax applies where authorized capital exceeds the minimum band)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands (Majuro) — submitted via the licensed Registered Agent in accordance with Association of Registered Agents (ARA) procedures
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before November 30 of each calendar year; no statutory extension is available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or non-payment after November 30 precipitates late fees, loss of good standing, and adverse registration status; sustained non-payment of franchise taxes over successive annual cycles exposes the corporation to administrative strike-off/dissolution by the Registrar, with reinstatement available only after payment of all arrears, assessed penalties, reinstatement fees, and possible surrender of the corporate name if reallocated during the lapse.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Registered Agent Due-Diligence Refresh and Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (ARA compliance cycle covering any shareholding transfers during the review year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Registered Agent; protocol administered under the rules of the Association of Registered Agents (ARA) of the Republic of the Marshall Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Refreshed annually in conjunction with the November 30 statutory filing cycle and updated within 30 days of any change in shareholders or beneficial owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government penalty applies; stale or incomplete beneficial ownership records constitute a breach of ARA regulatory requirements and Business Corporations Act record-keeping obligations, may prompt a compliance deficiency notice from the Registrar of Corporations, and can obstruct issuance of a Certificate of Good Standing or delay future dissolution/reinstatement requests.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandated for a non-resident, tax-exempt Business Corporation under the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act, and no turnover, asset, or employee thresholds trigger an audit for the payroll SaaS entity. A certified audit may nonetheless be required by external financing covenants, investor agreements, or a licensed banking/insurance/trust activity (not applicable to this scope), and would become mandatory if the corporation were reclassified as resident through business operations in the Marshall Islands.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No statutory accounting framework is prescribed for a non-resident Business Corporation; voluntary financial statements, when prepared for lenders or investors, should adopt one framework consistently (IFRS as issued by the IASB or US GAAP), include a basis-of-presentation disclosure, and are not subject to public filing in the Marshall Islands.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Marshall Islands does not operate a public beneficial ownership register. Under Association of Registered Agents (ARA) requirements, the licensed Registered Agent must obtain, verify, and retain current beneficial ownership information for the corporation, expressly covering any shareholding transfer completed during the year; the annual confirmation refresh is processed with the November 30 renewal cycle, and every change in the corporate register must be flagged to the Registered Agent within 30 days of the underlying transaction.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$650 - US$1,200 per year for a standard licensed Registered Agent, registered office, and annual ARA due-diligence administration; premium provider tiers or consolidated packages may reach approximately US$1,800.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$3,500 - US$9,000 for a voluntary certified audit of a typical holding-type payroll SaaS entity; not an obligatory expenditure unless required by a financing covenant, investor consent right, or an applicable regulatory licensing condition.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax exemption for non-resident business corporations: no corporate income tax, no capital gains tax, no branch profits tax, no payroll tax, and no property tax on foreign-sourced revenue. The only annual impost is the corporate registration/annual franchise fee levied by the RMI Registrar.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Statement of Entity Status (Annual Report) — filed electronically through the RMI Registrar of Corporations online portal (IRAG / Maritime Corporate Administrator e-filing system). No corporate income tax return exists because non-resident business corporations deriving no Marshall Islands-source income are outside the RMI Income Tax Act.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within the registration anniversary month; a 30-day grace period is extended by the Registrar. Failure to file within the grace period triggers a monthly late penalty and potential administrative dissolution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity legal name and registration number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the exact name stated on the Certificate of Incorporation; non-resident BCs must maintain an RMI registered agent for service of process.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered agent name and registered office physical address in the Marshall Islands
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident entity must appoint and maintain a registered agent in RMI; P.O. boxes are not permitted.
Directors may be non-residents; at least one director is required. Complete details are mandatory, but the register may be kept outside RMI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholders (names, share class, number of shares issued)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Bearer shares are prohibited; non-resident shareholders must be disclosed to the RMI registrar through the corporate register, despite beneficial ownership filings remaining confidential.
For payroll automation under ISIC 6201, describe the high-level business purpose: 'automated global payroll and staff compliance software provisioning'. No license is required.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of USD 100 per month or part thereof after the due date; failure to file for three consecutive months may result in administrative dissolution, requiring a reinstatement fee plus all outstanding fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — no Marshall Islands withholding tax on dividends paid by a non-resident business corporation to any shareholder, resident or non-resident.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: RMI has no comprehensive double taxation agreement network applicable to dividend streams from a domestic business corporation. As the statutory rate is 0%, no de facto treaty relief is required. Where an investor nonetheless holds a foreign tax credit position, the standard protocol is to obtain a true and certified certificate of residence (TRC) from the home-state authority and present it to the RMI corporate administrator solely for documentary support; no RMI withholding tax is assessed.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate: 0% for royalties and interest paid to non-residents. Treaty rate: 0% (no bilateral DTA reduction needed). No RMI withholding tax is imposed on payments of IP licence fees or debt interest by a non-resident BC to foreign creditors or licensors.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 0 — RMI imposes no transfer pricing documentation threshold because the non-resident business corporation is fully tax-exempt; however, any intercompany cross-border arrangement should still maintain contemporaneous arm's length evidence for substance verification and regulatory review.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Marshall Islands Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) apply to relevant entities that are RMI tax-resident and undertake relevant activities (e.g., credit business, financing and leasing, shipping, holding company as pure equity holding, headquarters, distribution and service centre). A non-resident BC operating a global payroll SaaS platform with central management and control outside RMI is ordinarily outside ESR scope. If any RMI-sourced service is undertaken, the entity must satisfy the mind-and-management test, maintain adequate premises and staff in RMI, and file an economic substance declaration annually.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Falsely declaring the entity as any of the following in annual filings: no RMI-source revenue, inactive status, or purely passive holding, while actually carrying on active business through an RMI office or deriving RMI-source income subject to Income Tax Act assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of RMI corporate income tax at 30% on taxable RMI-source income, plus interest of 1% per month and a civil penalty of up to 50% of the tax understated; registration and annual filing privileges may be revoked.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed the false statement may be personally liable for the unpaid tax penalty where they knowingly suppressed revenue or false-declared non-residence; a criminal conviction carries a fine of up to USD 10,000 and imprisonment not exceeding 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating without economic substance, holding assets solely to circumvent creditor enforcement, or being interposed in a scheme for treaty abuse or trade-based money laundering despite the absence of any licensable activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act and ESR, the Registrar may strike the company from the register, order its dissolution, and refer the facts to the Attorney-General; equity courts may pierce the corporate veil, rendering the corporation and its directors liable for third-party debts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly and severally liable for fraudulent trading and are subject to a director disqualification order of up to 10 years. If cross-border fraud is alleged, directors may face extradition to the RMI and an asset freeze in foreign jurisdictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the RMI non-resident BC as an anonymised conduit for receiving payroll funds, wage disbursement surcharges, or biometric staff compliance data where the beneficial owner is not disclosed, or transacting with sanctioned persons on the RMI consolidated sanctions list.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The RMI Crimes Act and AML/CFT framework impose monetary penalties of up to USD 1 million per violation on the entity; the financial regulator may ban the entity from receiving remittances and revoke the corporate registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individual directors who knowingly authorise, direct, or fail to prevent prohibited transfers face imprisonment of up to 12 years, personal seizure of the funds concerned, and a travel ban until the investigation is completed. Voluntary self-disclosure to the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit materially reduces criminal exposure.
